title: Switching to trombone, Lambert, Welch and joining the Silver Leaf Band
summary: Umphrey advises a trombone; the band breaks up and reforms under Henry Lambert and Frank Welch, who brings them to Albert Batiste's Silver Leaf Band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: About one mile and a quarter out of the city limit. And we used to have to meet Professor Umphrey every Sunday morning about 9 o'clock. We had a little road cart. We'd carry him, flurry and two. And so the people that I wait for, they give us a place that we could have our practice, take our lessons, and might near every night while we was there playing and doing the best that we could. And so Professor Umphrey, I had to take him back in for it. And he advised me to buy a trombone. And I agreed to do so. And he bought me a trombone, paid eight dollars for it, a silver bell, a method, and a catechism. So I would take bass violins on Sunday. And during the week one day, I would come to his house on Liberty Street in New Orleans with my trombone. He told me that it wasn't much, no difference in the music much. Just you had to learn the precessions and learn how to blow. And I thought that was very good. And a little while after that, this band broke up. And probably about two months later, there was an old man by the name of Lambert, Henry Lambert. He was an old musician, old tuba player. And he organized this bunch again. And he played the vowel trombone this time in the band. And we had another professor then by the name of Frank Welch, one of the old coinette players, and his son was the drummer. So then he played. We had two coinettes then in the band. And he taught us and played coinette along with us. And later, this band broke up.
